instruction: Use this as an internal visual judgment layer. Do not surface the full checklist to the user unless asked.

hard_fail_any: main subject is unclear on mobile first view
page feels like a stack of components rather than a designed page
shared footer or navigation overwhelms the page purpose
cards are used where typography, rules, rows, or tables would be better
Japanese copy becomes unnatural because of a design or style rule
visual treatment looks generic AI template or SaaS template

axes.label: First view composition
axes.question: Does the first screen immediately communicate the page role and main subject
axes.score_5: Single clear subject, controlled nav, no secondary block steals attention
axes.score_3: Subject is present but competing UI blocks dilute it
axes.score_1: The viewer sees support UI, cards, or footer-like elements before the real subject

axes.label: Visual hierarchy
axes.question: Are title, lead, body, links, and secondary elements weighted correctly
axes.score_5: A clear typographic ladder and restrained emphasis guide reading
axes.score_3: Hierarchy works but too many blocks compete

axes.label: Negative space
axes.question: Does the page breathe without becoming empty or padded
axes.score_5: Space creates editorial calm and premium rhythm
axes.score_1: Space is used as padding around unnecessary cards

axes.label: Component restraint
axes.question: Are cards, wrappers, CTAs, navs, and related blocks actually needed
axes.score_5: Most design value comes from typography, rules, rhythm, and strong content order
axes.score_3: Some unnecessary components remain but do not dominate
axes.score_1: The page is a stack of cards, wrappers, and black blocks

axes.label: Scroll rhythm
axes.question: Does the page feel intentional while scrolling
axes.score_5: Each section changes rhythm without adding noise

axes.label: Mobile order
axes.question: Does mobile order match the real user task
axes.score_5: Hero, useful content, action, and secondary notes appear in the correct order
axes.score_3: Main content appears but supporting blocks interrupt
axes.score_1: Form, profile subject, article body, or main page purpose appears too late or out of order

axes.label: Footer and nav weight
axes.question: Do shared layout elements remain subordinate
axes.score_5: Footer and nav support the page without changing its perceived purpose
axes.score_3: Footer or nav is heavy but tolerable
axes.score_1: Footer or nav visually overwhelms the page

axes.label: CBJ fit
axes.question: Does the visual language feel like a premium automotive editorial media site
axes.score_5: Quiet, confident, car-media appropriate, not generic
axes.score_1: Feels like a generic dashboard, SaaS site, agency template, or legal template

decision_labels.adopt: Use the pattern directly after CBJ translation
decision_labels.adapt: Use only the underlying visual logic
decision_labels.reject: Do not use for this CBJ page type
decision_labels.delete: Remove existing UI rather than replacing it
